evidence_labels.V: Read directly from the source (text, transcript, description, manual, API) and, where a verifier ran, confirmed by it.
evidence_labels.A: Approximate: read from low-resolution YouTube storyboard frames; consistent with the source but digits not legible.
evidence_labels.U: Unverified: single community claim, search snippet, illegible value, inferred key mapping or conflicting sources.
evidence_labels.D: Derived by the pitwall synthesis (arithmetic or inference). Not a published value.
evidence_labels.H: pitwall heuristic threshold (rig_check only). Unsourced; calibrate on recorded captures before giving advice.

conventions.setting_value: Every setting is an object {value, min, max, evidence, as_published?, note?}. A single published value goes in 'value'; a published range goes in 'min'/'max' (value null, or a suggested start marked with its own evidence in the note). 'as_published' keeps the source's short label (e.g. 'PEAK', 'Off or <=5').
conventions.off_encoding: For numeric Tuning Menu parameters whose range starts with OFF (FF advanced, NDP, NFR, NIN, INT, FOR, SPR, DPR, FUL, BLI), OFF is encoded as 0 with as_published 'OFF'. Enum parameters (FFS, SHO, MPS, AP, SEN AUTO) use their enum string.
conventions.absent_or_na: value null with as_published 'N/A' or 'not shown' means the setting does not exist in that configuration.
conventions.platform: 'platform' is the platform pitwall offers the preset on and is always one of games[].platforms. 'applies_to_platforms' lists every platform the values are valid for. 'source_platform' is where the source author configured it: pc | ps5 | ps4 | xbox | pc_ps5 (shared column) | playstation (PS4/PS5 not stated) | not_split (one table for all platforms) | not_stated. 'ps5_reachable' is true when every wheel/in-game key can be set on PS5 (Tuning Menu + game menu).
conventions.torque: 'torque_nm' is the torque of the source's own hardware or design target (null if not stated). 'applies_to_torque_nm' lists the GT DD Pro torques the values may be used at (filter on this). 'torque_basis': source_states | source_says_both | source_does_not_distinguish | inferred.
conventions.pedals: 'pedals' is the pedal model the source used (a hardware.pedals id) or null; 'pedals_basis': source_states | source_shows (storyboard) | inferred | not_stated. Pedal-model-specific values (BRF, BLI) live in 'pedal_settings' and only transfer to the models in 'transferable_to_pedals'. In-game brake/throttle calibration keys are game params flagged pedal_dependent.
conventions.versions: 'game_version.id' is the game build the preset was made on (games[].versions). 'game_version.predates' lists later FFB-relevant builds. 'firmware.era' is a hardware.wheel_bases[].firmware_eras id: the source's own firmware era when the source shows it (era_basis source_shows), otherwise the newest era that existed at publication (era_basis publication_date). 'stale' is true when a later game build is known to invalidate the values; 'status' is current | stale | superseded | not_for_ps5.
conventions.preference: 'preference' is one of realism | competitive | balanced | comfort | official_default. 'preference_basis' = source_words when the source's own wording supports it, inferred when pitwall classified it.
conventions.verified_flag: sources[].verified = an adversarial verifier re-checked this source in the 2026-10-10 research round; false = read only by the researcher (gap-fill pass or guidance). It says nothing about value precision: see values_evidence and per-value evidence.

firmware_eras.label: Fanatec Control Panel / FanaLab driver era and early Fanatec App, base firmware before 1.8
firmware_eras.changes: All 2025 sources. Endstop scaled with FF on CSL DD / GT DD Pro.

firmware_eras.label: Last pre-FullForce firmware
firmware_eras.changes: BRF reset after base restart fixed; endstop independent of FF; ClubSport DD/DD+ holding torque raised. 1.8.1.7 is the downgrade target some users chose for the F1 25 v1.25 oscillation bug.

firmware_eras.label: FullForce firmware for CSL DD / GT DD Pro
firmware_eras.changes: FUL (FullForce) added at 5 and 8 Nm; Boost Kit holding torque 6 -> 8 Nm (peak stays 8); FFS Peak/Linear no longer offered with the Boost Kit (App 1.5.1.2 changelog); NFR shaking fixed. Base shutdowns hotfixed in 1.5.2.3 (interim advice FFB <= 75 for Boost Kit users, superseded). Known issues: DPR weaker than intended, endstop scaling with FF.

firmware_eras.label: DPR/NDP correction
firmware_eras.changes: DPR behaviour corrected; grainy feel at high NDP fixed; endstop no longer scales with FF. GT7 1.71 instability appeared on this firmware.

firmware_eras.label: GT7 1.71 hotfix firmware (current)
firmware_eras.changes: Fixes FFB loss, oscillation and shutdowns after GT7 1.71 and menu-exit oscillation (R3E/rF2/BeamNG). The 1.5.4.x notes list no firmware numbers; 1.9.2.3 arriving with 1.5.4.x is inferred from the 1.6.1.3 table. Current as of 2026-10-10. App 1.6.1.3 known issues: FullForce weaker than intended on CSL DD/GT DD Pro; GT DD Pro can lose FFB in GT7; SPR/DPR not working in GT7 menus; set SEN manually for F1 games.

params.label: Tuning Menu profile (A SET / C SET / 1 SET-5 SET)
params.range: Standard menu: A SET + C SET (one custom). Advanced menu: A SET + 1 SET..5 SET
params.meaning: A SET hands the values to a supporting game and locks them (wheel shows LOCKED). GT7 uses it (re-tuned in 1.71); F1 25 use is undocumented. Custom slots are stored in the base and save every change at once. Hold Tuning ~4 s to toggle Standard/Advanced (FAQ says 3 s); hold ~6 s more to reset the custom slots (returns to Standard). The Standard menu shows only SEN, FF, NDP, SHO, MPS and BRF, so every official preset needs the Advanced menu and a custom slot. On PS5 the values GT7 pushes to A SET can be read by scrolling the on-wheel menu and copied into a custom slot (GTPlanet RS60NR).

params.label: Operating mode (power-button LED)
params.range: DARK BLUE = PlayStation native (PS5/PS4); PURPLE = PS4 compatibility (appears as CSL Elite WB+ PS4); RED = PC native (firmware, Fanatec App); YELLOW = PC compatibility (appears as ClubSport WB V2.5); GREEN = Xbox (needs an Xbox-licensed rim)
params.default: unverified (persistence across reboots and firmware updates not documented by Fanatec)
params.meaning: Short-press the power button to cycle. Use DARK BLUE for F1 25 and GT7 on PS5; PURPLE only for old titles that do not detect the GT DD Pro. USB update rate up to 250 Hz in PlayStation mode (manual). Firmware updates need RED mode on a Windows PC; Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 shows a prompt asking PlayStation/Xbox-mode users to switch to PC mode.

params.label: Sensitivity (steering rotation)
params.range: Standard: 180-1080 or AUTO; Advanced: 90-2520 or AUTO
params.meaning: Total rotation. A fixed value overrides the game; AUTO lets the game set it per car (GT7 does; otherwise the 2520 deg electronic limit applies). For F1 games set it manually and equal to the in-game Maximum Wheel Rotation (Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue with AUTO in F1 games, seen on PC; Fanatec's 2026 F1 page says AUTO may not work on some platforms; a PS5 DD+ owner keeps a dedicated F1 slot with 360).

params.label: Force Feedback (max motor strength; 'FFB' on Fanatec web pages and the wheel display)
params.meaning: Scales all game FFB relative to the base's maximum torque (5 Nm PEA / 4 Nm LIN on the 90 W PSU; 8 Nm with the Boost Kit 180), so the same FF gives up to 1.6x the torque after the Boost Kit [D]. Fanatec manual/help: get stronger feedback from FF rather than in-game strength to avoid clipping. Endstop strength is independent of FF on current firmware (fixed in App 1.4.2.3, regressed in 1.5.2.3, fixed again in base FW 1.9.1.1). FF 63 at 8 Nm reproduces the 5 Nm torque map [D].

params.label: Force Feedback Scaling
params.meaning: PEA = full peak torque; LIN = lower maximum, steadier holding force (4 Nm on the standard PSU, ~6 Nm with the Boost Kit). If an 8 Nm base shows 6 Nm, FFS is LIN.
params.availability: Present at 5 Nm (still shown in the Fanatec App at 5 Nm on FullForce firmware [A]). ABSENT with the Boost Kit from base FW 1.9.0.2 (Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 changelog: Peak/Linear no longer offered with the Boost Kit; holding torque raised 6 -> 8 Nm) [V]. Conflict: Fanatec help articles 30312080999825 / 50420340753297 (updated Sept 2026) still describe LIN/PEAK. Check the menu once the kit is fitted.

params.label: Natural Damper
params.meaning: Damping driven by steering speed/acceleration; Fanatec's first fix for oscillation and wheel speed in oversteer. Higher = calmer and heavier, slower rotation, less fine detail. Values below 25 need the Advanced menu. Base FW 1.9.1.1 fixed graininess at high NDP. Raising NDP does not prevent the F1 25 v1.25 session-change oscillation (reported at NDP 50 / INT 11).

params.label: Natural Friction
params.meaning: Simulated friction of steering parts. Can calm oscillation; high values cost responsiveness and detail.

params.label: Natural Inertia
params.meaning: Simulated steering mass, useful with light rims; smooths NFR on direction changes. Small amounts stop oscillation starting; too much sustains it once started.

params.label: FFB Interpolation filter
params.meaning: Filters/interpolates the game FFB signal; OFF = raw, 20 = heaviest. Fanatec F1 25 uses 3; Fanatec's oscillation guide keeps 1-5. The legacy FAQ default 6 applies to older bases, not the GT DD Pro.

params.label: Force Effect Intensity
params.meaning: Sharpness of force effects: 000 smoothest, 100 sharpest. Fanatec F1 25: lower to 90 or 80 if harsh; Fanatec GT7: keep as high as possible.

params.label: Force effect modifier (constant force)
params.meaning: Scales the game's constant-force (main steering) channel. Above 100 amplifies, can clip and heats the motor. Fanatec: keep 100 and set strength in game; 80-90 only to reduce fatigue. Values 1-9 are not selectable. Fanatec F1 25 lists N/A on Xbox.

params.label: Spring effect modifier
params.meaning: Scales the game's spring (centring) channel; some games use it to centre the wheel in menus. Low/OFF stops the base re-centring after centre calibration. Known issue (App 1.6.1.3): SPR and DPR do not work in the GT7 menu on the GT DD Pro.

params.label: Damper effect modifier
params.meaning: Scales the game's damper channel (inferred to include F1 25 Wheel Damper). Weaker than intended in App 1.5.2.3; corrected in base FW 1.9.1.1, so DPR advice from before 2026-08-11 may feel different.

params.label: FullForce strength
params.range: OFF-100 (Fanatec documents the range for Podium DD / CS DD / CS DD+; GT DD Pro range unverified)
params.meaning: High-frequency FullForce layer, effective only in titles that implement it. Fanatec's FullForce games list (2026-02-10) names iRacing, GT7 and AC EVO; GT7 enabled it on the GT DD Pro in 1.71. No source shows F1 25 / 2026 Season Pack implements FullForce: treat FUL as having no effect in F1 25 [U]. Added to CSL DD / GT DD Pro by base FW 1.9.0.2 (App 1.5.1.2), at 5 and 8 Nm. GT7 users read and set it on the PS5 Tuning Menu. Known issue (App 1.6.1.3): strength lower than intended on CSL DD / GT DD Pro.

params.label: Brake Level Indicator
params.meaning: Pedal vibration at a brake-input threshold. Only with ClubSport Pedals V3/V3i: NOT usable with CSL Pedals or the CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit. Presets that set BLI therefore used ClubSport V3 pedals.

params.label: Shock (vibration motors)
params.meaning: Turns vibration motors in a connected Fanatec rim/pedal on or off; shown only when such a device is connected. CSL Pedals and the LC kit have none; bundled GT DD Pro rim motors unverified. Old presets using 'SHO 100' (0-100 scale) cannot be set on this base.

params.label: Multi Position Switch mode
params.meaning: Output mode for rotary switches. Not supported by the bundled GT DD Pro rim.

params.label: Analogue paddles mode
params.meaning: Clutch bite point, clutch/handbrake, brake/throttle or mappable axes. Not supported by the bundled GT DD Pro rim. Some sources print it as 'ACP'.

params.label: Power supply / max torque (hardware state, not a menu item)
params.range: 90 W PSU: 5 Nm (FFS PEA) / 4 Nm (LIN); Boost Kit 180 (180 W): 8 Nm peak, holding 8 Nm on base FW >= 1.9.0.2 (6 Nm before; ~6 Nm with FFS LIN on older firmware)
params.default: per bundle (user: 5 Nm now, Boost Kit 180 arriving)
params.meaning: The Boost Kit 180 replaces the PSU; the base detects it and releases the torque automatically (no setup step documented). Only the original PSU or the Boost Kit 180 may be used. Fanatec rates 5 Nm for rims up to ~35 cm; heavier rims benefit from 8 Nm. No Fanatec thermal-derating data for the GT DD Pro at 8 Nm.

pedals.name: Fanatec CSL Pedals (stock, 2 or 3 pedals)
pedals.note: Correction to the project brief: the stock brake is not a potentiometer. Fanatec specifies 12-bit contactless Hall sensors on throttle and brake; the brake measures position (travel).

params.label: Sensor type
params.default: 12-bit contactless Hall sensors on throttle and brake
params.meaning: Position (travel) based brake with a stiffer spring plus PU foam for a progressive feel. No BRF and no manual calibration.

params.label: Auto-calibration routine
params.meaning: After every power-on press throttle and brake fully once and release before driving; until then max/min readings can be wrong. Manual calibration needs the Load Cell Kit.

params.label: Connection
params.meaning: On console the pedals work only through the Fanatec wheel base. No USB without the LC kit or a ClubSport USB adapter.

pedals.name: Fanatec CSL Pedals + CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit

params.label: Brake Force (set in the wheel base Tuning Menu)
params.meaning: Pedal force needed for 100% brake; Lo = least force, 100 = most. Over RJ12 it acts as the brake maximum. Shown in the Standard and Advanced menus once the LC brake is detected. Fanatec states only 'approx. 10 kg minimum' sensitivity and gives no kg mapping or maximum. Community measurement (super_gt, possibly Fanatec-affiliated): ~60 kg at the pedal face reaches 100% at BRF MAX on a stock kit. Linear interpolation (10 kg at 010, 60 kg at 100) is an unverified assumption [D]. BRF values do not transfer between Fanatec pedal models. BRF reset bugs: fixed in 2022 drivers, again in App 1.4.2.3 (May 2026); 'BRF shown as 0% in the App' known issue fixed in 1.6.1.3.
params.menu: both (once the LC brake is detected)

params.label: Manual Mode min/max calibration
params.meaning: Fanatec Control Panel/App on Windows only; values saved to the pedal's internal memory; reset by an LC firmware update. A CSL LC owner on PS5 set deadzones once on a laptop and they persisted on PS5 (GTPlanet Abarth_71) [U: Fanatec does not state PS5 persistence].

params.label: Auto-calibration routine
params.meaning: Without Manual Mode press each pedal fully after power-on, then release; a community note says to hold max for 2-3 s, and that brake values drift during a session if this is skipped. If the brake reads input at rest: firmware update plus pedal reset via PC (Fanatec help 50374908960273).

params.label: Wiring
params.range: RJ12 accelerator 'Wheel Base / Load Cell' port -> LC 'Load Cell' port; accelerator -> base
params.meaning: Never connect RJ12 and USB at the same time. Update base firmware before installing. The old brake can be refitted as a clutch. On PS5 the LC kit works only through the base.

params.label: Load Cell Kit hardware
params.default: 12-bit load cell; 65 Shore elastomer stack; ~10 kg minimum sensitivity; firmware 1.8 (App 1.6.1.3)
params.meaning: Capacity in kg is not published. The '90 kg' figure often attached to it is Fanatec's CSL Elite Pedals V2 load cell, not this kit. No Fanatec tuning elastomers are sold for it.

pedals.name: Fanatec ClubSport Pedals V3 / V3i (reference only)

params.label: Brake Force (ClubSport V3)
params.meaning: Different load cell and range from the CSL LC Kit; values do not transfer.

params.label: Brake Level Indicator (base Tuning Menu; needs CSP V3 vibration motor)
params.meaning: Same key as the wheel base BLI parameter.

pedals.name: Fanatec CSL Elite Pedals + CSL Elite Load Cell Kit (V1) (reference only)

params.label: Brake Force (CSL Elite LC)
params.range: current Tuning Menu article: Lo, 010-100; old manual OFF..100 with contradictory direction text
params.meaning: Manual elastomer table: 65 Shore up to ~20 kg = BRF Lo-40; 85 Shore up to ~40 kg = Lo-70; 95 Shore up to ~90 kg = full range. Some 2019-2020 firmware inverted the direction. Does not transfer to the CSL Pedals LC Kit.

pedals.name: Fanatec CSL Elite Pedals V2 (reference only)

params.label: Brake Force (CSL Elite V2)
params.meaning: Load cell rated up to 90 kg (Fanatec Explorer 2025-11-11); elastomers 65/75/85 Shore. Does not transfer to the CSL Pedals LC Kit.

pedals.name: Load-cell brake, model not shown by the source (reference only)

params.label: Brake Force (model unknown)
params.meaning: BRF scales differ per Fanatec model; values from an unknown model do not transfer.

versions.label: F1 25 launch, 2025 cars
versions.notes: Fanatec F1 25 page (2025-07-01) and most 2025 presets.

versions.label: 2026 Season Pack (v1.20), 2026 cars
versions.notes: Active Aero reuses the DRS binding; Overtake reuses the 2025 mapping; Fanatec published new (conflicting) values.

versions.label: v1.25
versions.notes: S Mode/DRS stays active only while throttle > 90%; closer input-to-physics match for wheels during rapid input changes; fix for FFB calls limiting frame rate; Moza/Simucube stability. Introduced FFB oscillation/loss after a session change on Fanatec CSL DD / GT DD Pro (EA confirmed; fix shared with Fanatec 2026-10-07, no ETA). Players on several brands report lighter/less detailed FFB.

versions.label: v1.26
versions.notes: Career crash fix only; does not fix the v1.25 oscillation.

params.label: Settings Filter
params.section: Settings (toggled with Triangle from the Controls screens)
params.meaning: How many options the menus show. Set Expert if wheel options are missing.

params.label: Vibration & Force Feedback
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Master switch for wheel FFB and vibration. Community PS5 report (unverified): toggling it restores FFB lost mid-race.

params.label: Vibration & Force Feedback Strength
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.range: 0 to above 100 (110, ~115 and 120 observed; maximum unverified, ~150 suggested by slider proportions)
params.meaning: Overall game FFB gain; main weight control. F1 25 has no clipping meter and no published measurement of game-side clipping against this value exists. If F1 25 sends a normalised force command (undocumented for PS5), game-side clipping depends on this value and car/track load, not on base torque [D]. Same-author sources give the same value at 5 and 8 Nm; game version moved values more than torque (Carson at 8 Nm: F1 24 55-70, F1 25 75-90, v1.25+ 90-100).

params.label: On Track Effects
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Canned road-surface texture added on top of physics FFB. Not listed on Fanatec's 2026 page.

params.label: Rumble Strip Effects
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Canned kerb vibration.

params.label: Off Track Effects
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Canned grass/gravel effects.

params.label: Pit Stop Effects
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Vibration during pit stops; no driving effect.

params.label: Wheel Damper
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Game-side damping/weight; stacks with base NDP and is scaled by DPR. More damping hides some FFB detail. Consensus 0-3. Do not use it to fight the v1.25 session-change oscillation.

params.label: Maximum Wheel Rotation
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Vibration & Force Feedback
params.meaning: Physical degrees mapped to full in-game lock; below 360 steering gets quicker. Set base SEN to the same number.

params.label: Steering Rate
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 100% on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; wheel default unverified
params.meaning: How fast stick input reaches maximum lock (aimed at analogue sticks). Wheel guides leave 100%.

params.label: Steering Deadzone
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Initial rotation ignored. Keep 0 on direct drive.

params.label: Steering Linearity
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Makes the centre less sensitive. SimRacingSetup suggests ~5; most wheel sources 0.

params.label: Steering Saturation
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Full lock reached before full physical rotation. Keep 0 unless the wheel cannot reach full lock.

params.label: Throttle Deadzone
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Initial travel ignored. Raise only if telemetry shows throttle above 0 at rest.

params.label: Throttle Linearity
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Less sensitive start of travel (wheelspin control without TC). Wheel sources use 0.

params.label: Throttle Saturation
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: 100% reached before full travel. Since v1.25 S Mode/DRS stays active only while throttle > 90%: use a small value only if the pedal cannot reach ~1.0.

params.label: Brake Deadzone
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Initial travel (force with a load cell) ignored. Use 1-3 only if telemetry shows brake at rest or DRS closing; check it does not swallow trail-brake input.

params.label: Brake Linearity
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 25 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot; Opmeer (PC, Fanatec) says 25 by default; PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: Less sensitive start of the pedal. Sources split: 0 (Carson), 3 (F1withNick), 25 (Opmeer, THOMB). No CSL LC owner report for F1 25 exists. Raise if small touches lock the wheels; the Joyce et al. 2025 study links a steep low-end response with harder trail braking.

params.label: Brake Saturation
params.section: Controls, Vibration & Force Feedback > [wheel preset] > Calibration
params.default: 0 on EA's F1 25 gamepad screenshot (RacingGames' '25% default' claim contradicted); PS5 wheel-preset default unverified
params.meaning: 100% brake reached with less travel/force; raises sensitivity and cannot cap output below 100%. Fix the range in hardware first (BRF, calibration).

params.label: Brake Pressure (car setup)
params.section: Car Setup (per car); UDP CarSetups m_brakePressure
params.meaning: Brake force delivered for a given pedal input. Lower it if you lock too easily; too low costs braking (Trophi/Driver61). The PS5-reachable lock-margin lever in F1 25.

params.label: Overtake ERS Mode
params.section: Controls - Generic (global)
params.meaning: Hold deploys only while held; Toggle switches on/off. In 2026 content it governs Overtake on the same mapping.

params.label: Telemetry Settings: UDP Telemetry / IP Address / Port / Format
params.section: Settings > Telemetry Settings
params.meaning: Must be On and pointed at the pitwall host for the rig check and UDP Action presses. pitwall parses formats 2025 and 2026.

params.label: UDP Action 1-12
params.section: Controls > [wheel preset] > UDP Custom Actions
params.meaning: Effect only in UDP: Event 'BUTN' buttonStatus bits 0x00100000 (Action 1) to 0x80000000 (Action 12). pitwall radio PTT uses Action 1. Use a spare button (sharing with a driving action unverified).

params.label: Activate/Deactivate DRS/S Mode
params.section: Controls > [wheel preset] > Control Scheme
params.default: L2 in EA's PlayStation wheel example (Logitech G923); GT DD Pro pre-mapped default unverified
params.meaning: DRS (2025 cars) or Active Aero Straight Line Mode (2026 cars); reuses the DRS binding. Since v1.25 stays active only while throttle > 90%.

params.label: Overtake/Boost
params.section: Controls > [wheel preset] > Control Scheme
params.default: R2 in EA's PlayStation wheel example (G923); GT DD Pro default unverified
params.meaning: 2026 Overtake Mode / manual Boost; reuses the 2025 Overtake mapping.

params.label: Push to Talk (game voice commands)
params.section: Controls > [wheel preset] > Control Scheme
params.meaning: The game's own voice commands, separate from pitwall's radio PTT on a UDP Action.

versions.label: 1.15 (temporary wheel FFB cut)
versions.notes: Presets from this window (Max. Torque 10, FOR 120) were compensation values.
FFB algorithm uses the full torque range; Auto Setup re-tuned for GT DD Pro / GT DD Extreme / Podium.

FFB torque strength and friction, understeer vibration and wheel throttle/brake input characteristics changed; ABS behaviour changed; Auto Setup re-tuned; FullForce enabled on the GT DD Pro. A DG Edge headline (unverified) dates GT7 Spec IV Part 1 to 2026-10-15: re-check after it.

params.label: Force Feedback Max. Torque
params.section: Quick Menu > Settings > Controller Settings > Steering Force Feedback
params.meaning: Game scale, not Nm, reportedly non-linear (high values compress). Higher = duller tyre response in hard cornering. Pre-1.71 presets used 5-6 (3-7 by car class); post-1.71 community guidance 4-5 with A SET; post-hotfix 8 Nm reports 5-10 (no consensus).

params.label: Force Feedback Sensitivity
params.section: Quick Menu > Settings > Controller Settings > Steering Force Feedback
params.meaning: Resistance build-up at turn-in; higher reacts more to changes, lower is gentler on straights. Fanatec uses 1. Pre-hotfix disconnect/wobble reports link high values (5-10) with high torque and FUL.

params.label: Controller Steering Sensitivity
params.section: Controller Settings
params.meaning: Wireless controller only; no effect on a wheel.

params.label: Countersteering Assistance
params.section: Driving Options / Assists
params.range: Weak / Strong (Off used in Fanatec and SRS presets)
params.meaning: Auto-corrects oversteer. Fanatec sets Off for wheel users.

params.label: ABS
params.section: Driving Options / Assists
params.meaning: Changes how brake input turns into deceleration; record it for the brake rig check. 1.71 changed ABS behaviour.

params.label: Vibration (wheel; UNVERIFIED)
params.section: unverified
params.meaning: Post-1.71 GT DD Pro users list a Vibration value; one found disabling it removed FullForce effects. Not documented in the official manual pages checked.

params.label: Controller (pedal) calibration (UNVERIFIED)
params.section: GT Menu > Options > Controllers (claimed)
params.meaning: Community claim (GTPlanet RS60NR, 2025-01-06, pre-1.71) that GT7 can store pedal min/max/deadzone; contradicts the 2022 Fanatec forum statement that GT7 has no pedal deadzone. CSL LC owners set deadzones in Fanatec PC software instead. Verify on the user's PS5.

recommendations.description: Setup output for this rig. Look up wheel[game, torque_nm, preference] and pedals[game, pedals, preference], then merge: wheel_settings from the wheel entry, pedal_settings from the pedal entry, ingame_settings = wheel entry + pedal entry (pedal entry wins on brake/throttle calibration keys). Apply 'rules' when the hardware changes. Entries with sourced=false are explicit no-source entries: either derived values (evidence D) or empty with fallback_to.
common_steps: Put the base in DARK BLUE mode. Hold the Tuning button ~4 s for the Advanced menu and pick a custom slot (suggested: 1 SET = F1 25, 2 SET = GT7 custom, 3 SET = experiments). Do not use A SET for F1 25.

Firmware needs a Windows PC with the base in RED mode and the Fanatec App. Update before fitting the Boost Kit or the LC kit; afterwards switch back to DARK BLUE, recalibrate the wheel centre and recheck slot values. The mobile app does not currently work with the Windows App.
F1 25: set SEN to the same number as Maximum Wheel Rotation (do not rely on AUTO); check the 90-degree alignment visually.
Stock CSL Pedals and LC kit without Manual Mode: after every power-on press each pedal fully once (hold the brake at max 2-3 s) and release before driving.
F1 25 calibration baseline: steering deadzone/linearity/saturation 0; throttle 0/0/0; brake deadzone 0 and brake saturation 0; brake linearity per the pedal recommendation.
Change one thing at a time on a fixed car/track and record it next to the capture.
F1 25 v1.25 known bug: if the wheel oscillates or loses FFB after a session change (e.g. Qualifying to Race), pause and power-cycle the base. Do not tune NDP/INT/damper to fight it.

rules.rule: When moving from 5 Nm to 8 Nm keep FF 100 and the same VIB_FFB_STRENGTH. Every same-author source gives the same in-game value at both torques (SRS esports 80-100 at 5 and 8 Nm; SRS 70 built for 8 Nm, usable at 5; Fanatec one CSL DD/GT DD row of 80; Fanatec 2026 50-70 for every base). No source lowers in-game strength going from 5 to 8 Nm. Forces become up to 1.6x stronger; game-side clipping is unchanged if F1 25 sends a normalised command [D].
For comfort, scale VIB_FFB_STRENGTH by 5/8 (about x0.63) to keep the 5 Nm weight, then adjust by feel.

For an exact A/B against the old 5 Nm feel, set FF 63 at 8 Nm with unchanged in-game values; this reproduces the 5 Nm torque map, including its clipping. Endstop strength does not depend on FF on current firmware.

Base FW >= 1.9.0.2 raised Boost Kit holding torque from 6 to 8 Nm, so long high-load corners feel heavier than 8 Nm presets made on older firmware. If the first sessions are tiring, lower in-game strength in steps of 5-10 or use the comfort entry.
With the Boost Kit on base FW >= 1.9.0.2 FFS is not offered (Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 changelog). Set FFS PEA only if the menu still shows it (LIN gives ~6 Nm).
Presets made before v1.25 (2026-09-07) may feel lighter after it (player reports; Carson raises strength by 10-20 at 8 Nm). Start at the upper end of a published range, then adjust by feel.

Hands-off oscillation on straights: raise NDP in steps of 5 first, keep INT 1-5, then lower strength, then a little NFR; NIN with care (Fanatec oscillation guide). With NDP OFF at 8 Nm expect to need NDP 5-20 [U]. Oscillation starting at a session boundary in F1 25 v1.25+ is a known game bug, not a settings fault.
Fanatec's GT7 values are stated to suit 5 and 8 Nm. After fitting the kit restart at Max. Torque 5 (or 4-5 with A SET) and step up; post-hotfix 8 Nm reports range 5-10 with no consensus.
FUL default 100 on hotfix firmware (App >= 1.5.4.2). If FFB drops out or the base disconnects: FUL 60, then OFF; then leave 10-20% headroom (FF 80-90) and lower Sensitivity.

rig_check.description: Maximum brake input while throttle >= 0.95 on straights. Ghost braking can close DRS / S Mode.
rig_check.action_if_high: Hall pedals: press-fully routine after power-on, check mechanics. Load cell: check elastomer/piston preload; firmware update + pedal reset via PC (Fanatec help 50374908960273). Then F1 25 BRAKE_DEADZONE +1..3 and confirm trail-brake input is not swallowed.

rig_check.description: Per-lap minimum throttle input; detects a throttle that never returns to 0.
rig_check.action_if_high: Press-fully routine after power-on; F1 25 THROTTLE_DEADZONE +1..2; check the return spring.

gt7: throttle byte 0x91 (may be post-TCS; judge with TCS off)

rig_check.description: p99 of throttle input on straights. Since F1 25 v1.25 (2026-09-07) S Mode/DRS stays active only while throttle input is above 90%.
rig_check.action_if_low: Press-fully routine after power-on; small THROTTLE_SATURATION; check the mechanical stop.

sources.author: EA SPORTS / Codemasters (F1 25 v1.25 patch notes)

rig_check.description: Median peak brake of braking events whose entry speed is above 250 km/h (event = non-zero brake run with peak > 10%, >= 120 zero frames either side at 60 Hz, adapted from Joyce et al. 2025).
rig_check.action_if_low: Hall pedals: press-fully routine; small BRAKE_SATURATION. Load cell: lower BRF so a firm, repeatable press reaches 100%. If the peak collapsed suddenly at an unchanged BRF, see brake_peak_vs_history.

rig_check.description: Percentage of braking time with brake >= 0.99, plus count of flat tops >= 0.99 lasting > 0.3 s in low-speed zones. Long plateaus mean the pedal mapping saturates and modulation range is lost.
rig_check.good_range: <= ~30% of braking time overall; no flat tops concentrated in low-speed corners with lock-ups [H]
rig_check.action_if_high: Load cell: raise BRF. Both: BRAKE_SATURATION back to 0, add BRAKE_LINEARITY, lower car-setup BRAKE_PRESSURE; technique: bleed off as downforce falls.
rig_check.action_if_low: If peaks also fall short of 0.95, follow brake_peak_heavy_zones.

rig_check.description: TPB: time from brake onset to maximum per braking event (Joyce et al. 2025). Reference values are ACC GT3, not F1.
rig_check.good_range: close to the driver's own best laps; ACC GT3 reference 0.31-0.38 s
rig_check.action_if_high: Hesitant or segmented application (Coach Dave): coach a faster initial application in high-downforce stops.

rig_check.description: TBD: time from the last frame at peak brake to zero per event (Joyce et al. 2025). Trail-braking duration ranks among lap-time predictors (Hojaji et al.).
rig_check.good_range: close to the driver's own best laps; ACC GT3 reference 0.94-1.26 s
rig_check.action_if_low: Abrupt release: try a less sensitive start (BRAKE_LINEARITY) and coach a progressive release; re-check after the Load Cell Kit (the load cell gave longer TBD in Joyce et al.).

rig_check.description: Braking events where brake falls by >= 10 points then rises by >= 10 points before release (peak-release-reapply).
rig_check.action_if_high: Braking too early or modulation trouble (HP Academy); review pedal mapping (BRF / linearity) and technique.

rig_check.description: Share of front lock-ups (F1 MotionEx m_wheelSlipRatio / m_wheelSpeed; sign and units to confirm on a recording) that start with brake >= 0.99. Log brake value and rate, speed, steer, m_brakePressure, m_brakeBias and the ABS flag at onset.
rig_check.action_if_high: Mapping too sensitive: raise BRF (load cell), lower car-setup BRAKE_PRESSURE, add BRAKE_LINEARITY.
rig_check.action_if_low: Lock-ups at partial brake late in the zone point to technique (not bleeding off as downforce falls), not the pedal.

rig_check.description: F1 only: count of m_drs 1 -> 0 transitions while 0 < brake < 0.05 (ghost brake closing DRS / S Mode).
rig_check.action_if_high: As brake_at_rest_max: recalibrate, fix mechanics, then a small BRAKE_DEADZONE.

rig_check.description: Rise of the per-event peak brake over the first heavy stops of a session at a similar entry speed (median of stops 1-3 vs stops 8-10). Fanatec pedals auto-calibrate on use; a rising peak means the press-fully routine was skipped after power-on.
rig_check.action_if_high: Do the press-fully-then-release routine (hold the brake at max 2-3 s) after every power-on; with the LC kit consider PC Manual Mode.

sources.author: Fanatec (CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit manual)

rig_check.description: Load cell: standard deviation of brake input during near-constant holds (>= 0.3 s with |d brake/dt| small) compared with the driver's usual. A jittery signal under constant pressure was reported on a CSL LC.
rig_check.action_if_high: Hardware/firmware issue, not a BRF reason: check wiring (never RJ12 + USB together), firmware, elastomer seating.

rig_check.description: Load cell: session median of heavy-stop peaks compared with the driver's history at the same BRF. A sudden collapse (one owner topped out at ~30% at BRF 70) or light pressure reading full brake are fault signatures.
rig_check.good_range: within 0.10 of the driver's history at the same BRF [H]
rig_check.action_if_high: Light pressure reads full brake: possible damaged load cell (Fanatec staff reply on a CSL Elite LC); contact support.
rig_check.action_if_low: Sudden collapse at unchanged BRF: hardware/firmware fault or BRF reset; recheck BRF on the wheel (BRF reset bugs fixed in App 1.4.2.3), update firmware, then contact support. Do not compensate by lowering BRF.

rig_check.description: Share of lap time with |m_steer| >= 0.99 outside slow hairpins (GT7: wheel rotation radians vs configured lock).
rig_check.good_range: ~0 outside hairpins (Monaco hairpin needs ~21-22 deg road-wheel lock vs ~17 deg normally) [H]
rig_check.action_if_high: In-game rotation set too low for the driver's inputs, or STEERING_SATURATION > 0; check SEN equals MAX_WHEEL_ROTATION.

rig_check.description: |median m_steer| on straights with low yaw rate.
rig_check.action_if_high: Recalibrate the wheel centre on the base (also needed after firmware updates); check STEERING_DEADZONE.

rig_check.description: Fit of F1 m_steer against MotionEx m_frontWheelsAngle (radians); with STEERING_LINEARITY 0 the relation should be linear with no kink near centre.
rig_check.action_if_low: A kink near centre reveals steering linearity or deadzone settings; set them to 0 unless intended.
